x: The Speaker's office is in Part V (the Union), mainly Articles 93–96, 100, 110 and 118. Part VI covers the States, where the Assembly Speaker sits.
t: Discriminate Part V (Parliament) from Part VI (State Legislatures).

x: Under Article 93, the Lok Sabha elects its Speaker from among its own sitting members. Neither the President nor the Prime Minister chooses the Speaker.
t: Recall who elects each presiding officer of Parliament.

x: Option B is incorrect. There is no six-month relaxation for the Speaker, who must already be an elected Lok Sabha member when chosen. That relaxation applies only to Ministers.
t: Discriminate the Minister's six-month rule from the Speaker's eligibility.

x: The Speaker takes no separate oath as presiding officer, only the oath taken as an ordinary MP. Options B and C invent an oath of office.
t: Remember that presiding officers take no separate oath of office.

x: The Lok Sabha Secretariat works directly under the Speaker's control and guidance, not under the executive, which keeps the House independent.
t: Recall who controls each House's secretariat.

x: Both are true: under Article 96, the Speaker cannot preside while a resolution for their own removal is considered, even if present. R gives the rule behind A.
t: Recall the Article 96 bar on presiding.

x: Both are true: under Article 100, the Speaker does not vote in the first instance in normal sittings, but gives a casting vote when votes are tied.
t: Discriminate a first-instance vote from a casting vote.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: In normal parliamentary sittings, the Speaker does not vote in the first instance.
Statement B: In normal parliamentary sittings, the Speaker may exercise a casting vote in case of equality of votes.

Which of the following is correct?

x: A is true: during their own removal, the Speaker may speak, take part and vote in the first instance. B is false because no casting vote is allowed then, the reverse of normal sittings.
t: Contrast the Speaker's voting rights in normal and removal sittings.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: During consideration of the Speaker's own removal resolution, the Speaker may speak and take part in the proceedings.
Statement B: During such consideration, the Speaker may exercise a casting vote in case of a tie.

Which of the following is correct?

x: The Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker and the Deputy Speaker to the Speaker, under Article 94(b). The resignation goes sideways, not up to the President. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Remember that the two presiding officers resign to each other.

x: Option D is incorrect: the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution but stays until just before the new Lok Sabha first meets.
t: Recall the Speaker's continuity after dissolution.

x: I and II are correct: under Article 94(c), the Speaker is removed by a majority of all the then members (an effective majority), after 14 days' notice. III is false because a simple majority is not enough.
t: Discriminate effective majority from simple majority.

x: The Speaker presides over a joint sitting (Article 118(4)), then the Deputy Speaker, then the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman. Money Bill certification is under Article 110(4). The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the order of who presides over a joint sitting.

x: All four belong to the Speaker: adjourning or suspending the House when there is no quorum (one-tenth, Article 100), adjourning sine die, and fixing the Deputy Speaker's election date under Rule 8(1).
t: Check each item for whether the Speaker or the President does it.

x: Both are true: the Speaker decides defection disqualifications under the Tenth Schedule, and Kihoto Hollohan (1992) made that decision subject to judicial review. Review is a check on the power, not its source, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether judicial review explains who holds the power.

x: Under Rule 8(1), the Speaker fixes the date for electing the Deputy Speaker. The President fixes only the Speaker's election date.
t: Discriminate who fixes the Speaker's and the Deputy Speaker's election dates.

x: The regular Speaker rests on Article 93 and is elected by the House. The Pro-Tem Speaker rests on Article 95(1) and is appointed by the President. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Discriminate the regular Speaker (Article 93) from the Pro-Tem Speaker (Article 95(1)).

x: A is true: by convention, the Pro-Tem Speaker is usually the senior-most member of the new House. B is false because the office ends as soon as the regular Speaker is elected.
t: Remember the Pro-Tem Speaker's office is temporary.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Pro-Tem Speaker is usually the senior-most elected MP of the newly elected House.
Statement B: The office of the Pro-Tem Speaker continues after the regular Speaker is elected.

Which of the following is correct?

x: The Pro-Tem Speaker administers the oath to new MPs and presides over the election of the regular Speaker. The Pro-Tem Speaker neither presides till dissolution nor certifies Money Bills.
t: Discriminate the Pro-Tem Speaker's temporary tasks from the regular Speaker's powers.

x: Mavalankar was the first Speaker (1952–56), Meira Kumar the first woman Speaker (2009), Sumitra Mahajan the second (2014, 16th Lok Sabha) and Om Birla Speaker of the 17th Lok Sabha (2019). The order is B, C, A, D.
t: Place each Speaker by the Lok Sabha in which they were elected.
s:
Arrange the following milestones in chronological order:
A. Sumitra Mahajan becomes the second woman Speaker
B. G.V. Mavalankar serves as the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha
C. Meira Kumar becomes the first woman Speaker
D. Om Birla becomes Speaker of the 17th Lok Sabha

x: The Speaker is covered by Articles 93–96 (election, vacation, removal), 100 (casting vote), 110 (Money Bill certificate) and 118 (joint sitting rules).
t: Recall the Speaker's Articles: 93–96, 100, 110 and 118.

x: Option B is incorrect: the Pro-Tem Speaker is appointed by the President under Article 95(1), not elected by the House. The Pro-Tem Speaker is usually the senior-most member and serves until the regular Speaker is elected.
t: Discriminate appointment by the President from election by the House.

x: Both are true: the regular Speaker is the House's regular presiding officer, and enforcing its rules and conducting business is what that role consists of. R explains A.
t: Ask whether R describes the work that makes A true.

x: Only I is correct: the regular Speaker is elected by the Lok Sabha. II is false because the Pro-Tem Speaker swears in the newly elected MPs; III is false because appointment by the President applies to the Pro-Tem Speaker.
t: Separate the duties of the Pro-Tem Speaker from those of the regular Speaker.

x: Mavalankar was the first Speaker (1952–56), Meira Kumar the first woman Speaker and Sumitra Mahajan the second, so the answer is a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.
t: Match the first Speaker and the two women Speakers in order.

x: Statement A is false: the Pro-Tem Speaker, not the regular Speaker, swears in the newly elected MPs. Statement B is true: the Pro-Tem Speaker also conducts the election of the regular Speaker.
t: Discriminate the Pro-Tem Speaker's two tasks from the regular Speaker's role.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The regular Speaker administers oath to newly elected MPs.
Statement B: The Pro-Tem Speaker enables the election of the regular Speaker.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Three are the Speaker's: adjourning sine die, deciding Tenth Schedule disqualifications, and fixing the Deputy Speaker's election date. The President, not the Speaker, appoints the Pro-Tem Speaker.
t: Find the item done by the President.

x: Option C is incorrect. Under Article 110(4), the Speaker alone certifies a Money Bill, and the certificate is final when the Bill goes to the Rajya Sabha and to the President. The Rajya Sabha cannot overrule it.
t: Remember that the Speaker's Money Bill certificate is final.

x: In normal sittings, the Speaker may speak and take part in the proceedings. Voting is different: the Speaker does not vote in the first instance and has only a casting vote.
t: Discriminate the right to speak from the right to vote.

x: The Deputy Speaker's office is in Part V, Articles 93–96, the same Articles as the Speaker's. Part VI covers State Legislatures.
t: Remember the Speaker and Deputy Speaker share Articles 93–96.

x: Under Rule 8(1), the Speaker fixes the date of the Deputy Speaker's election, and the Secretary-General informs the members.
t: Discriminate who fixes the date from who communicates it.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Constitution does not require the Deputy Speaker to come from the Opposition. Choosing an Opposition member is only a parliamentary convention.
t: Discriminate a convention from a constitutional requirement.

x: Like the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker takes no separate oath as presiding officer, only the oath taken as an ordinary MP.
t: Remember that presiding officers take no separate oath of office.

x: The President fixes the Speaker's election date and the Speaker fixes the Deputy Speaker's. Each resigns to the other, so the answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Pair the dates first, then the cross-addressed resignations.

x: Under Article 94(b), the Deputy Speaker resigns to the Speaker, not to the President or the Prime Minister.
t: Remember that the two presiding officers resign to each other.

x: Option B is incorrect: removing the Deputy Speaker needs an effective majority (a majority of all the then members), not two-thirds, after 14 days' notice.
t: Discriminate effective majority from special majority.

x: Both are true: Article 96 bars the Deputy Speaker from presiding while their own removal is considered, even if present. R explains A.
t: Recall the Article 96 bar on presiding.

x: While presiding, the Deputy Speaker has the Speaker's powers, and their rulings cannot be appealed to the Speaker. The Deputy Speaker presides over joint sittings when the Speaker is absent and chairs any committee they are appointed to. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall each of the Deputy Speaker's special privileges.

x: All three are correct: when not in the Chair, the Deputy Speaker is an ordinary member who can debate, move motions and vote in the first instance, unlike the Speaker.
t: Contrast the Deputy Speaker's position off the Chair with the Speaker's.

x: I, II and III are correct: during their own removal, the Deputy Speaker cannot preside but may speak, take part and vote in the first instance. IV is false because no casting vote is allowed then.
t: Find the statement giving a casting vote in removal proceedings.

x: Three are common to both: Article 93, election by the House, and no separate oath. Only the Speaker stays in office after dissolution; the Deputy Speaker vacates at once.
t: Find the feature that belongs only to the Speaker.

x: When appointed to a Parliamentary Committee, the Deputy Speaker automatically becomes its Chairman, one of the office's special privileges.
t: Recall the Deputy Speaker's committee privilege.

x: No appeal lies to the Speaker against a ruling the Deputy Speaker gives from the Chair, because while presiding the Deputy Speaker has the Speaker's full powers.
t: Recall the status of the Deputy Speaker's rulings.

x: The Speaker resigns to the Deputy Speaker and the Deputy Speaker to the Speaker; either is removed by an effective majority after 14 days' notice; on dissolution the Speaker stays in office until just before the new House first meets.
t: Remember that the two presiding officers resign to each other.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Speaker's resignation
(b) Deputy Speaker's resignation
(c) Removal of the Speaker or the Deputy Speaker
(d) Speaker's office on dissolution of the Lok Sabha

List-II
(i) Effective majority of the Lok Sabha after 14 days' notice
(ii) Addressed to the Speaker
(iii) Addressed to the Deputy Speaker
(iv) Continues until just before the new House first meets

x: Both are true: removing the Deputy Speaker needs a majority of all the then members, which R names and defines as an effective majority, as distinct from simple and special majorities. R explains A.
t: Recall the three kinds of majority and where each is used.

x: The Speaker fixes the Deputy Speaker's election date under Rule 8(1), and the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha communicates it to all members.
t: Discriminate who fixes the date from who communicates it.

x: Under Article 93, the Lok Sabha elects the Deputy Speaker from among its own sitting members. Nominated or Rajya Sabha members are distractors.
t: Recall that both presiding officers are elected from sitting members.

x: I, II and IV are correct: the office is in Part V, Articles 93–96, and the Deputy Speaker takes the oath only as an ordinary MP. III is false because there is no separate oath of office.
t: Find the statement inventing a separate oath.
s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha:
I. The constitutional framework relating to the office is contained in Part V.
II. Articles 93 to 96 relate to the office and its associated provisions.
III. The Deputy Speaker has a separate oath of office as presiding officer.
IV. The Deputy Speaker takes oath solely as an ordinary Member of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Article 93 provides the office, 94(b) resignation, 95 powers while presiding, and 96 the bar during one's own removal, so the answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Remember that Articles 93–96 run in order: office, vacating office, powers, removal.

x: On dissolution, the Speaker stays in office until just before the new House first meets, while the Deputy Speaker vacates office at once. That continuity protects only the Speaker.
t: Discriminate what happens to each presiding officer on dissolution.

x: Under Articles 64 and 89(1), the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). The Deputy Chairman is elected from its members.
t: Recall the office that brings the Rajya Sabha chairmanship with it.

x: Under Article 89(2), the Rajya Sabha chooses its Deputy Chairman from among its own members, so the Deputy Chairman is a member, unlike the Chairman (the Vice-President).
t: Discriminate the non-member Chairman from the member Deputy Chairman.

x: Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, Nehru the Union Constitution Committee, Rajendra Prasad the Rules of Procedure Committee, and J.B. Kripalani the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall each Constituent Assembly committee's chairman.

x: Patel chaired the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals, H.C. Mukherjee the Minorities Sub-Committee, B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya the House Committee and Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar the Credentials Committee.
t: Recall the chairs of the Constituent Assembly's minor committees one by one.
s:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I
(a) Advisory Committee on FRs, Minorities, Tribals
(b) Minorities Sub-Committee
(c) House Committee
(d) Credentials Committee

List-II
(i) B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya
(ii) H.C. Mukherjee
(iii) Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
(iv) Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar

x: The Drafting Committee under Ambedkar was set up on 29 August 1947. 23 June 1947 is the Flag Committee's date and 26 November 1949 the adoption of the Constitution.
t: Discriminate between the Constituent Assembly's dates.

x: Option C is incorrect: the States Committee, which negotiated with the princely States, was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru. Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee and the Advisory Committee; Mavalankar chaired the Functions Committee.
t: Do not credit Patel with every States-related committee; Nehru chaired the States Committee.
o: The Union Powers Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru and dealt with federal subject distribution.
The Steering Committee was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad and dealt with steering Assembly business.
The States Committee was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and dealt with negotiations with the princely States.
The Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.

x: Both are true: the Speaker appoints the PAC Chairman, and since 1967 that Chairman has by convention come from the Opposition. Who appoints does not explain the convention, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether the appointing authority explains the convention.

x: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha. Option B reverses the split.
t: Recall the PAC's 15 + 7 split.

x: The Estimates Committee is the largest parliamentary committee, with 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha. The PAC and Public Undertakings Committee have 22 members each.
t: Discriminate the 30-member Estimates Committee from the 22-member committees.

x: Option A is incorrect: the convention, since 1967, of an Opposition Chairman applies to the Public Accounts Committee. The Public Undertakings Committee has 22 members (15 + 7), and the Speaker appoints its Chairman.
t: Discriminate which committee follows the Opposition-Chairman convention.

x: The President appoints the UPSC Chairman and the Governor the State PSC Chairman; Parliament prescribes the Finance Commission members' qualifications by law; the Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee.
t: Match each body to who appoints, who prescribes, or who chairs.
s:
Match the body with the relevant authority.

List-I
(a) Appointment of the UPSC Chairman
(b) Appointment of the State PSC Chairman
(c) Qualifications of Finance Commission members
(d) Chairperson of the Lokpal Selection Committee

List-II
(i) Governor of the State
(ii) President of India
(iii) Prime Minister
(iv) Parliament by law

x: Both are true: a State PSC Chairman appointed by the Governor can be removed only by the President, and removal for misbehaviour needs a Supreme Court inquiry under Article 317. The inquiry is the procedure, not the reason the power lies with the President, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether R gives the reason for A or just a related procedure.

x: K.C. Neogy was the first Chairman of the Finance Commission (1951). Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar and Ambedkar were Constituent Assembly figures.
t: Recall the first Finance Commission chairman.

x: I, II and III are correct: the Finance Commission has five members, the President appoints them, and Parliament prescribes their qualifications by law. IV describes the PAC.
t: Find the statement borrowed from a parliamentary committee.
s:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:
I. It consists of five members, including the Chairman.
II. The President appoints the Chairman and members.
III. Parliament prescribes their qualifications by law.
IV. The Finance Commission has 22 members, comprising 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Option B is incorrect: the Rajya Sabha Chairman is not on the Lokpal Selection Committee. It has the Prime Minister (chair), the Lok Sabha Speaker, the Leader of the Opposition, the CJI or a nominated judge, and an eminent jurist.
t: Recall the five members of the Lokpal Selection Committee.

x: Both are true: the Estimates Committee's Chairman traditionally comes from the ruling party, and the Speaker appoints the PAC's Chairman.
t: Discriminate the Estimates Committee and PAC chairmanship conventions.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Estimates Committee is traditionally chaired by a member from the ruling party.
Statement B: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Three were chaired by Rajendra Prasad: the Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag, the Rules of Procedure Committee and the Steering Committee. The States Committee, which negotiated with the princely States, was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
t: Remember the States Committee went to Nehru, not to Rajendra Prasad.

x: The Union Powers Committee handled federal subjects, the Functions Committee the Assembly's operations, the Provincial Constitution Committee the provinces, and the Order of Business Committee the daily agenda. The answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
t: Match each committee name to the subject it suggests.

x: Article 64 makes the Vice-President ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States, and Article 89(1) restates it in Part V.
t: Recall Articles 64 and 89(1).

x: Nehru chaired the Union Constitution Committee, as well as the Union Powers Committee and the States Committee.
t: Recall the committees chaired by Nehru.

x: Both are true: the Functions Committee handled the Assembly's operational functions, and the Rules of Procedure Committee its procedural rules.
t: Match each committee to the subject its name suggests.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Constituent Assembly Functions Committee dealt with the operational functions of the Assembly.
Statement B: The Rules of Procedure Committee dealt with the Assembly’s procedural rules.

Which of the following is correct?

x: G.V. Mavalankar chaired the Functions Committee, Rajendra Prasad the Rules of Procedure Committee, Nehru the States Committee and K.M. Munshi the Order of Business Committee. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Pin down Munshi and Mavalankar first; the major committees went to Nehru and Prasad.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) Committee on the Functions of the Constituent Assembly
(b) Rules of Procedure Committee
(c) States Committee
(d) Order of Business Committee

List-II
(i) K.M. Munshi
(ii) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
(iii) G.V. Mavalankar
(iv) Jawaharlal Nehru

x: The Ad-hoc Committee on the National Flag was set up on 23 June 1947. The Drafting Committee followed on 29 August 1947.
t: Discriminate between the Constituent Assembly's dates.

x: I and II are correct: Patel chaired the Advisory Committee and the Provincial Constitution Committee. III is false because J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee; H.C. Mukherjee chaired the Minorities Sub-Committee.
t: Discriminate between the two sub-committees' chairmen.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
II. The Provincial Constitution Committee was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
III. The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by H.C. Mukherjee.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members, 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, like the PAC.
t: Recall the 15 + 7 split shared with the PAC.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members.
Statement B: The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

Which of the following is correct?

x: Three are correct: the PAC and Public Undertakings Committee each have 15 Lok Sabha and 7 Rajya Sabha members, and the Estimates Committee is drawn only from the Lok Sabha. Statement 4 is false because it has 30 members.
t: Discriminate the 30-member Estimates Committee from the 22-member committees.

x: Both are true: Parliament prescribes Finance Commission members' qualifications by law, which is why the President does not. R explains A.
t: Ask whether R names who holds the power A denies the President.

x: The President appoints the Finance Commission under Article 280, but Parliament sets its members' qualifications by law (Finance Commission Act, 1951).
t: Discriminate who appoints from who prescribes qualifications.

x: The UPSC conducts the Civil Services Examination; the State PSC Chairman is appointed by the Governor; the Finance Commission is constituted every five years under Article 280; the Prime Minister chairs the Lokpal Selection Committee.
t: Use the feature unique to each body to fix the pairs.
s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(a) UPSC
(b) State PSC
(c) Finance Commission
(d) Lokpal Selection Committee

List-II
(i) Constituted every five years under Article 280
(ii) Conducts the Civil Services Examination
(iii) Chairman appointed by the Governor
(iv) Prime Minister as Chairperson

x: All four are members of the Lokpal Selection Committee, with the Prime Minister as its chair: the Speaker, the Leader of the Opposition, the CJI or a nominated judge, and an eminent jurist.
t: Recall the five members of the Lokpal Selection Committee.
s:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal Selection Committee:
I. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is a member.
II. The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha is a member.
III. A Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court judge nominated by the Chief Justice of India is a member.
IV. An eminent jurist is a member.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: Both are true: the President appoints the UPSC Chairman (Article 315) and removes them, and removal for misbehaviour needs a Supreme Court inquiry (Article 317). The inquiry is a procedure, not the reason for the power, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a procedure explains who holds the power.

x: Patel chaired the 1931 Karachi Congress Flag Committee. Rajendra Prasad chaired the separate 1947 Constituent Assembly Flag Committee.
t: Discriminate the 1931 Congress committee from the 1947 Constituent Assembly committee.

x: Both are true: the Drafting Committee had seven members and prepared the draft Constitution. Its task does not explain its size, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a committee's task explains its size.

x: Both are true: the Advisory Committee under Patel was the parent body, and its Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee under Kripalani worked out the rights in detail.
t: Discriminate the parent committee from its sub-committees.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribals was the parent overarching advisory committee.
Statement B: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee dealt with the detailed formulation of fundamental rights.

Which of the following is correct?

x: All three are correct: the Minorities Sub-Committee dealt with minority safeguards, the House Committee with accommodation, and the Finance and Staff Committee with staff and budget.
t: Match each committee to the subject its name suggests.
s:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Minorities Sub-Committee dealt with minority safeguards.
II. The House Committee dealt with residential and Assembly accommodations.
III. The Finance and Staff Committee dealt with internal staff and budget matters.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

x: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha appoints the Estimates Committee's Chairman, as for the PAC and the Public Undertakings Committee.
t: Recall that the Speaker appoints the financial committees' chairmen.

x: The Union Constitution Committee under Nehru worked out the structure of the Union government. The Union Powers Committee, also under Nehru, dealt only with the distribution of subjects between the Union and the States.
t: Separate the Union's structure (Constitution Committee) from its subjects (Powers Committee).
s: Which Constituent Assembly committee, chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, dealt with the structure of the Union government, such as its executive and legislature?

x: A is true: under Article 280 the President constitutes a Finance Commission every five years or earlier. B is false because Parliament, not the President, prescribes the qualifications by law (Finance Commission Act, 1951).
t: Separate who constitutes the Commission from who prescribes qualifications.
s:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President every five years or earlier.
Statement B: The qualifications of the Finance Commission Chairperson and members are prescribed by the President.

Which of the following is correct?
